proof_summary: Quadratic reciprocity makes 5 a quadratic residue modulo such a prime \(p\); choosing a representative \(4\le m<p\) gives \(m^2-5=pt\) with \(t<m\). A continuant invariant shows that \(t\) divides the accompanying denominator (with the small cofactor cases handled separately), whereas divisibility by \(p\) would propagate through the recurrence to the terminal value \(-1\), so reduction cancels exactly \(t\) and leaves \(p\).
